newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish H1 Exchequer returns show 721mln punt surplus.
newsitem.headline: Irish H1 Exchequer returns show 721mln punt surplus.

text.p: Ireland's end-June Exchequer returns showed a surplus of 721 million Irish pounds compared with an Exchequer borrowing requirement of 455 million in the first half of 1996, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.
Analysts' forecasts had been for a surplus of 100 to 650 million punts.

An overall exchequer surplus at end-June had been expected on the basis of budget projections but the strength of tax receipts throughout the first half of the year combined with lower net expenditure than expected, due to timing factors, has resulted in the surplus being considerably higher than expected, Finance Minister Charlie McCreevy said in a statement.
He said that despite some expected slippage in expenditure, there will be a very significant improvement on the budget target EBR of 637 million pounds for 1997.
The minister said he expected the EBR for the full year to be less than 300 million pounds.
The figures showed current budget surplus is 969 million against a deficit of 205 million at the end of the first quarter of 1997.
Total current receipts are 7,251 million in the first six months of the year.
All tax heads are performing "very satisfactorily" and are expected to exceed the budget target in almost every case, the minister's statement said.
Income taxes are especially buoyant, suggesting continuing growth in employment.
Tax revenue is expected to exceed the budget target by about 500 million pounds.
Exchequer borrowing for capital purposes totalled 248 million in the first half of 1997 compared with a deficit of 250 million in the same period of 1996.

"Although the pattern of receipts and expenditure will mean that there is likely to be a deficit overall at the end of the year, the cumulative surplus to date is a significant achievement which I would hope to build on over the coming years," McCreevy said.
The minister said the returns confirmed that Ireland would meet the Maastricht criteria for membership of EMU.
